forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: A 21% rally to $300 by March is entirely probable once buyers panic over depleted reserves and compounding climate shocks across Mediterranean producers.

forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Structural grain scarcity and Gulf offtake deals leave European spot buyers exposed to rapid price surges if winter weather disrupts Northern Hemisphere crops.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: The crowd stands at 28%. Wheat has trended upward over late summer, nudging our probability up marginally with the crowd.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: A spike above $300 requires a full corridor shutdown or export ban. Feasible given weaponized grain trade, but lower probability than $272.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Surpassing $300/mt requires extreme supply disruptions, though persistent Black Sea maritime risks provide an ongoing upside tail risk.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Reaching $300 requires extreme, prolonged supply shocks, though escalating Black Sea conflict and input costs keep upside risks real for European grain markets.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Severe heat and drought expose fragile monocultures to price spikes, though $300 remains a high hurdle without a catastrophic multi-region harvest failure.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: While the ag complex is in an easing-fueled upswing, clearing $300 requires extreme macro tailwinds. Market price is slightly overambitious.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Reaching $300/mt requires major systemic harvest failure. Exporter supplies remain sufficient to prevent an extreme price spike by spring 2027.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Our arable balance sheets indicate adequate supplies and above-average cereal yields, which reliably cap major price spikes toward $300/mt.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: A surge past $300/mt requires systemic trade barriers or major export bans. While Black Sea risks persist, global grain flows adapt and cap extreme rallies.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Skeptical of big bullish calls. Pushing past $300 requires severe sustained supply failure; typical weather and geopolitical spikes fade as supply responds.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: A surge above $300/mt would require an extreme stocks-to-use contraction that current global production estimates do not support.

forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Crossing $300 requires an extreme supply shock that markets inevitably overprice. High global output responses will cap rallies well before that threshold.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Reaching $300 by March requires an extreme rally before spring weather risks even materialize. Russian export flow and quiet winter dormancy will keep a firm lid on prices.

forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Spikes above $300 require extreme permanent shortages that ignore farmer adaptation, substitution, and rapid supply response.
